emma-peopleops: Hey all :wave: quick Q — I just enrolled in the 401(k) this morning. When should I expect deductions to actually start hitting my paycheck? Also, I have a partial vesting question from a previous employer — does rolling over affect my vesting timeline or match eligibility here?

mike-payroll: Hi Emma — welcome! TL;DR: deductions start on the first payroll after your enrollment clears payroll cutoff and the vendor is set up. Vendor setup + payroll mapping = usually 1–2 pay cycles. :calendar:

mike-payroll: Example payroll cutoff rules we use: 
```
- If enrolled by the 8th of the month -> effective on the end-of-month payroll (pay date ~ last business day)
- If enrolled after the 8th -> effective on next month's payroll
- Urgent changes submitted via payroll ticket can sometimes be applied mid-cycle but not guaranteed
```

jenna-hr-benefits: Adding context: vendor (e.g., our recordkeeper) typically needs 5–10 business days to create the account and accept deferral elections. That means even if payroll maps you in quickly, the vendor might not show the first contribution until the following deposit cycle. For most people that's 1–2 paychecks.

jenna-hr-benefits: Rollover from a previous employer does NOT reset your vesting schedule with us. Vesting for employer match is determined by each employer's plan rules. Your prior employer decides if old match was vested; rolling assets into our plan just moves balances. If you want to keep employer-match history separate, you can also leave it in the old plan — but that doesn't change Redwood's match schedule.

alex-eng: Quick follow-up: if I enable catch-up contributions (50+) or change deferral % mid-cycle, does that apply immediately or next pay?

mike-payroll: Catch-up flags and % changes need to be set before the payroll close for the pay period. If you file the change before cutoff (see dates above) it'll apply to that run; otherwise it applies next run. Also make sure to indicate "pre-tax" vs "Roth" in the benefits portal — payroll uses that flag for tax withholding.

emma-peopleops: @jenna-hr-benefits thanks — good to know rollover doesn't impact Redwood vesting. If someone wants to pause contributions temporarily (e.g., personal cashflow), any gotchas on match or taxable events?

jenna-hr-benefits: You can pause contributions any time via the benefits portal. Match is calculated only on contributions made while you're employed and enrolled, so pausing means less match dollars earned. No tax penalty for pausing contributions itself. If you pause and then leave before the next match vesting milestone, you might miss match dollars that would have vested.

mike-payroll: If anyone needs a fast change, file a payroll ticket with subject: "401k deferral change - urgent" and include: employee ID, effective pay date, deferral %, pre-tax vs Roth. We can escalate but can't promise mid-payroll edits after funds submission.

payroll-bot: FYI — next scheduled payroll run: 1830001400. Submit changes before cutoff (1830001300) to be considered for that run. :robot_face:

emma-peopleops: Awesome, super helpful — thanks everyone :thumbsup: I submitted enrollment before cutoff so I'll keep an eye on next paycheck and follow up if the vendor hasn't received it in 10 business days.

alex-eng: tagging this thread for teammates who asked earlier. Saved me a ticket. :clap:
